# Worked example: southern hake

This chapter fits the sex-structured model to a real, strongly dimorphic stock: southern hake
(*Merluccius merluccius*, ICES hke.27.8c9a). Females grow much larger than males (Linf 110 vs
74 cm), so the catch of large fish is almost all female. The inputs come from the Stock
Synthesis (SS3) assessment, which also gives a benchmark. The chapter

1. compares the sex-structured model with a one-sex model that ignores the sex structure, at the
   life history of the SS3 assessment;
2. estimates life-history parameters of both sexes with penalties;
3. shows what these fits tell the SS3 assessment.

## Data from the SS3 assessment

`data(hake)` holds the inputs built from the SS3 output with r4ss and ss3diags2
(`inst/extdata/make_hake.R`):

```{r hk-data}
data(hake)
names(lfd_hake)
ss3_hake$mirror
ss3_hake$sex_minlen
```

* **Fisheries:** trawlers (retained and discarded fish), volpal (longline), artisanal and
  cdTrw (a small trawl fleet). SS3 has quarterly length compositions; they are raised to annual
  catch at length with the SS3 catch numbers by season and partition, as FLicc expects for
  samples spread over the year.
* **Surveys:** SpSurv and PtSurv are sexed; CdSurv is unsexed.
* **CPUE fleets:** the two indices of the assessment mirror the selectivity of trawlers and volpal
  and have no length data, so their selectivity is that of these fisheries; they are not separate
  FLicc gears (and would enter the planned FLicc-SPM model through these gears).
* **Small fish not sexed:** in the sexed surveys the fish below 21 cm are not sexed. SS3 combines
  the sexes in those bins and stores them as females. `settings$sex_minlen` treats them the same
  way (chapter *Sex structure*); without it, the small fish would be read as a large excess of
  females.

```{r hk-lfd, fig.height = 5}
plot_lfd(FLQuants(lapply(lfd_hake[c("trawlers", "volpal", "artisanal", "PtSurv")],
                         function(q) q[, ac(2022:2024)])),
         type = "prop", sex_minlen = ss3_hake$sex_minlen)
```

## Life history by sex

The growth, maturity, weight and natural mortality are those of the SS3 assessment. Male growth
and M are set in SS3 as offsets from the females (male Linf = 110 × e^−0.4^ = 73.7 cm). M declines
with age in SS3; here it is M at length, `m_model = "inverse"`, $M(L) = M\,L_{ref}/L$ with
$L_{ref}$ = female L50, which follows the SS3 values within about 0.03 over the sizes caught.

```{r hk-lh}
lhpar_hake
stk_hake <- stocklen_sex(lfd_hake, lhpar_hake, m_model = "inverse")
```

```{r hk-lh-plot, fig.height = 3.5}
plot_growth(stk_hake, sex = "F") + ggplot2::ggtitle("Females")
plot_growth(stk_hake, sex = "M") + ggplot2::ggtitle("Males")
plot_m(stk_hake)
```

## Set-up

* The cdTrw fleet takes about 4% of the catch; its catch is added to the trawlers and its length
  data are not used.
* PtSurv is the survey: it is sexed, covers 15-50 cm and fits well. SpSurv mostly samples fish
  below 21 cm whose numbers vary with recruitment, and CdSurv is unsexed; both add little and are
  left out here.
* The fit uses the most recent 15 years, 2010-2024.

```{r hk-setup}
yy <- ac(2010:2024)
gears <- c("trawlers", "volpal", "artisanal", "PtSurv")
lfd <- FLQuants(lapply(lfd_hake[gears], function(q) q[, yy]))
cbg <- FLQuants(lapply(catch_hake, function(q) q[, yy]))
cbg$trawlers <- cbg$trawlers + cbg$cdTrw
cbg <- FLQuants(cbg[c("trawlers", "volpal", "artisanal")])
sf <- c(trawlers = "dsnormal", volpal = "logistic", artisanal = "dsnormal", PtSurv = "dsnormal")
set <- list(obs_model = "mn", surveys = "PtSurv", sex_minlen = ss3_hake$sex_minlen["PtSurv"])
ss3 <- data.frame(year = ss3_hake$spr$year, spr = ss3_hake$spr$spr)
ss3 <- ss3[ss3$year %in% 2010:2024, ]
```

## Sex-structured versus one-sex

The sex-structured fit uses the life history of both sexes; the one-sex fit uses the female life
history for all fish, with the survey sexes pooled. In both, female Linf has a weak penalty (SD 0.1
on the log scale) around the 110 cm of the assessment: with Linf fixed at exactly 110 cm the
one-sex model does not converge, a first sign that female growth alone does not fit these data.

```{r hk-fits}
fit_sex <- fiticc(lfd, stocklen_sex(lfd, lhpar_hake, m_model = "inverse"),
                  sel_fun = sf, catch_by_gear = cbg, settings = c(set, list(linf.sd = 0.1)))

pool1 <- function(q) { u <- unitSums(q); dimnames(u)$unit <- "unique"; u }
lfd1 <- FLQuants(lapply(lfd, pool1))
lhF <- FLPar(lhpar_hake@.Data[, "F", 1], params = dimnames(lhpar_hake)$params)
fit_one <- fiticc(lfd1, stocklen(lfd1, lhF, m_model = "inverse"), sel_fun = sf, catch_by_gear = cbg,
                  settings = list(obs_model = "mn", surveys = "PtSurv", linf.sd = 0.1))
rbind(convergence = c(sex_structured = fit_sex$opt$convergence, one_sex = fit_one$opt$convergence),
      female_Linf = round(c(fit_sex$obj$report()$Linf, fit_one$obj$report()$Linf), 1))
```

```{r hk-spr, fig.height = 4.5}
cmp <- list("Sex-structured" = fit_sex, "One-sex (female life history)" = fit_one)
plot_spr(cmp, ci = TRUE, ci_type = "ribbon") +
  ggplot2::geom_line(data = ss3, ggplot2::aes(x = year, y = spr), inherit.aes = FALSE,
                     linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.9)
```

The dashed line is the SPR of the SS3 assessment. Mean SPR by period:

```{r hk-spr-tab}
spr_tab <- function(fits) {
  x <- sapply(fits, function(f) c(f$report$spr))
  x <- cbind(SS3 = ss3$spr, x)
  round(rbind("2010-2014" = colMeans(x[1:5, , drop = FALSE]), "2015-2019" = colMeans(x[6:10, , drop = FALSE]),
              "2020-2024" = colMeans(x[11:15, , drop = FALSE])), 3)
}
spr_tab(cmp)
```

Ignoring the sex structure lowers SPR by about a third. With female growth only, the shortage of fish above about
75 cm, which in reality is the size only females reach, is read as fishing mortality; the
sex-structured model explains part of it by the males, which stop growing at about 74 cm.

Both FLicc fits follow the rise of SPR in the last years but stay below SS3. The stock has been
rebuilding from very high F: large females take many years to reappear in the length data, and an
equilibrium model reads their shortage as current fishing (chapter *Fishing mortality over time*).

The fits to the length data and the sex ratio at length in the survey:

```{r hk-len, fig.height = 6}
plot_len(fit_sex, year = 2022:2024)
```

```{r hk-sexratio, fig.height = 3.5}
plot_sexratio(fit_sex)
```

Below 21 cm the survey samples are one composition of both sexes (purple), above it female (red)
and male (blue). The observed proportion of females between 21 and 35 cm is below the
prediction: there are more males at these lengths than the male growth and M of the assessment
imply.

## Penalised estimates of the life history

Linf, M/k and CVL of each sex are fixed unless a penalty is given (chapter *Sex structure*). With
penalties (log-scale SD 0.1) centred on the SS3 values, the length data can move them. The
sex-structured fit above (female Linf penalised) is compared with fits at the SS3 values and with
male Linf or male M/k also estimated:

```{r hk-pen}
fit_fixed <- fiticc(lfd, stocklen_sex(lfd, lhpar_hake, m_model = "inverse"), sel_fun = sf,
                    catch_by_gear = cbg, settings = set)
pens <- list("Female and male Linf" = list(linf.sd = 0.1, linf_m.sd = 0.1),
             "Female Linf and male M/k" = list(linf.sd = 0.1, Mk_m.sd = 0.1))
fits_pen <- c(list("SS3 values" = fit_fixed, "Female Linf" = fit_sex),
              lapply(pens, function(p)
                fiticc(lfd, stocklen_sex(lfd, lhpar_hake, m_model = "inverse"), sel_fun = sf,
                       catch_by_gear = cbg, settings = c(set, p))))
lh_est <- function(f) {
  r <- f$obj$report()
  c(conv = f$opt$convergence, Linf_F = round(r$Linf, 1), Linf_M = round(r$Linf_m, 1),
    M_M_at_Lref = round(r$Mk_m * c(lhpar_hake["k", "M"]), 3),
    SPR_2024 = round(tail(c(f$report$spr), 1), 3), nll = round(f$opt$objective, 1))
}
t(sapply(fits_pen, lh_est))
```

```{r hk-pen-sexratio, fig.height = 3.5}
plot_sexratio(fits_pen[["Female Linf and male M/k"]])
```

```{r hk-pen-spr, fig.height = 4.5}
plot_spr(fits_pen) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(data = ss3, ggplot2::aes(x = year, y = spr), inherit.aes = FALSE,
                     linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.9)
```

The length data pull female Linf below the 110 cm fixed in the assessment (to about 92-96 cm),
which raises SPR, and male M below its SS3 value (males surviving better). A lower male M moves the
predicted sex ratio only slightly towards the observations: the remaining excess of males at
21-35 cm points to the male growth offsets or to a sex ratio at recruitment below 0.5. The changes
in the likelihood are a few units, so the penalties matter: the estimates show the direction the
length data point to, not values to adopt without other information (growth studies, tagging).

## Selectivity

The selectivity at length of the sex-structured fit against SS3 (dashed, females, 2024), and a fit
in which volpal is dome-shaped:

```{r hk-dome}
sf_dome <- sf; sf_dome["volpal"] <- "dsnormal"
fit_dome <- fiticc(lfd, stocklen_sex(lfd, lhpar_hake, m_model = "inverse"), sel_fun = sf_dome,
                   catch_by_gear = cbg, settings = c(set, list(linf.sd = 0.1)))
c(conv = fit_dome$opt$convergence, delta_nll = round(fit_dome$opt$objective - fit_sex$opt$objective, 1))
```

```{r hk-sel, fig.height = 5}
ss3sel <- ss3_hake$sel[ss3_hake$sel$gear %in% gears & ss3_hake$sel$len <= 90, ]
names(ss3sel)[names(ss3sel) == "len"] <- "L"
plot_compare_sel(list("Volpal logistic" = fit_sex, "Volpal dome" = fit_dome),
                 colours = c("#E69F00", "#0072B2")) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(data = ss3sel, ggplot2::aes(L, sel), inherit.aes = FALSE, linetype = 2)
```

```{r hk-dome-spr, fig.height = 4.5}
plot_spr(list("Volpal logistic" = fit_sex, "Volpal dome" = fit_dome),
         ci = TRUE, ci_type = "ribbon") +
  ggplot2::geom_line(data = ss3, ggplot2::aes(x = year, y = spr), inherit.aes = FALSE,
                     linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.9)
```

The length data clearly prefer a dome for volpal (lower negative log-likelihood). With the dome,
the shortage of large females is explained by large fish escaping the longlines rather than by
fishing, and SPR rises to the level of SS3, but the trend is lost in the early years. With all
gears dome-shaped nothing in the length data fixes how many large fish there are, so the dome and
F are confounded; the better fit may reflect the dome absorbing the shortage of large fish left by
past high F.

## What FLicc tells the SS3 assessment

FLicc fits each fleet's length data in seconds, with the same life history as the assessment, so
it is a quick check of structural choices:

* **Volpal selectivity:** the length data prefer a dome to the logistic curve of the assessment.
* **Female Linf:** the length data point to a smaller Linf than the 110 cm fixed in the
  assessment.
* **Male biology:** the sex ratio at length in PtSurv shows more males at 21-35 cm than the male
  growth and M offsets imply; a lower male M fits slightly better but does not explain all of it.
* **Sexed samples:** small unsexed fish must be combined over sexes (`settings$sex_minlen`, as in
  SS3), or they bias the male parameters.

Each is an SS3 sensitivity run (dome volpal, estimated Linf, male M and growth offsets).

**Limits.** The equilibrium model lags a rebuild, and length data alone cannot separate dome-shaped
selectivity from F. The CPUE indices of the assessment, which share the selectivity of trawlers
and volpal, carry exactly that information; combining them with the length data is the aim of the
planned FLicc-SPM model.
